document.title: Empty student directory
document.complaint: Students are registered, but the directory is empty.
document.business_rules: Show every student once with their department, ordered by student_id.

components.label: Student directory
components.query:
SELECT s.student_name, d.department_name
FROM Students s
JOIN Departments d
  ON s.student_id = d.department_id
ORDER BY s.student_id;
components.reference_query:
SELECT s.student_name, d.department_name
FROM Students s
JOIN Departments d
  ON s.department_id = d.department_id
ORDER BY s.student_id;

document.fault_cause: Student IDs and department IDs identify different entities. Join the student's department_id to the department's department_id.
checkpoints: Compare the Students records with the empty directory output.
Which column on Students identifies a department?
Match the foreign key for a student's department to the department's primary key.

scenarios.label: Visible
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Departments VALUES (10,'Engineering'),(20,'Business'); INSERT INTO Students VALUES (1,'Alice',20),(2,'Ben',10);

scenarios.label: Overlapping Ids
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Departments VALUES (1,'Science'),(2,'Arts'); INSERT INTO Students VALUES (1,'Dina',2),(2,'Eli',1);

scenarios.label: Shared Department
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Departments VALUES (7,'Law'),(9,'Design'),(12,'Unused'); INSERT INTO Students VALUES (30,'Same',7),(10,'Same',9),(20,'Noor',7);

alternative_repairs:
SELECT s.student_name, d.department_name
FROM Students s
JOIN Departments d
  ON s.department_id = d.department_id
ORDER BY s.student_id;

document.title: Missing residents
document.complaint: Some residents are missing from the support dashboard.
document.business_rules: Show every resident and their open-ticket count, including zero, ordered by resident_id.

components.label: Support dashboard
components.purpose: Shows residents and the count of their open support tickets.
components.query:
SELECT r.resident_id, r.resident_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS open_tickets
FROM Residents r
LEFT JOIN Tickets t
  ON r.resident_id = t.resident_id
WHERE t.status = 'OPEN'
GROUP BY r.resident_id, r.resident_name
ORDER BY r.resident_id;
components.reference_query:
SELECT r.resident_id, r.resident_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS open_tickets
FROM Residents r
LEFT JOIN Tickets t
  ON r.resident_id = t.resident_id
 AND t.status = 'OPEN'
GROUP BY r.resident_id, r.resident_name
ORDER BY r.resident_id;

document.fault_cause: WHERE removes residents with no open-ticket row. Filter status in the LEFT JOIN's ON clause so every resident remains. COUNT(t.ticket_id) ignores unmatched NULLs and returns zero.
checkpoints: Compare the Residents records with the single resident in the dashboard.
What happens to a LEFT JOIN row when its ticket columns are NULL and WHERE filters status?
Filter matching tickets in ON and count ticket_id so unmatched residents receive zero.

scenarios.label: Visible
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Residents VALUES (1,'Ava'),(2,'Ben'),(3,'Cara'); INSERT INTO Tickets VALUES (101,1,'OPEN'),(102,1,'CLOSED'),(103,3,'CLOSED');

scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Residents VALUES (30,'Same'),(10,'Same'),(20,'Dee'); INSERT INTO Tickets VALUES (201,10,'OPEN'),(202,10,'OPEN'),(203,10,'CLOSED'),(204,20,'CLOSED'),(205,20,NULL);

       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS open_tickets
